title: Free projective bundle agrees with base-change projective space
statement:
Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $r\geq0$ an integer. Let $F=\mathcal O_S^{\oplus(r+1)}$ with ordered basis $e_0,\ldots,e_r$, and let $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_S}(F)$ be its quasi-coherent symmetric algebra sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra], with symmetric grading [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded]. Write
$$p:\operatorname{Proj}_S(\mathcal B)\longrightarrow S$$
for relative Proj [def-nagata-relative-proj], equivalently the relative projective-space interface [def-nagata-relative-projective-space], and write
$$q:\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,r\};S)=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Proj}\mathbf Z[T_0,\ldots,T_r]\longrightarrow S$$
for the base-change projective space [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change, def-pc-fibre-product], with each $T_i$ of total degree one. There is a canonical scheme isomorphism
$$\theta:\operatorname{Proj}_S(\mathcal B)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,r\};S),\qquad q\circ\theta=p.$$
For every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$, its restriction, under the relative-Proj affine identifications, is the Proj comparison induced by the graded $R$-algebra isomorphism $\operatorname{Sym}_R(R^{\oplus(r+1)})\cong R[T_0,\ldots,T_r]$ sending $\iota(e_i)$ to $T_i$. These local comparisons agree with restriction on the base, whose polynomial coefficient maps fix every $T_i$.

proof.text: Use the already constructed affinePolynomialEquiv and affinePolynomial_homogeneous of [def-nagata-relative-projective-space]. Reindex its variables by ULift to obtain the graded R-algebra isomorphism R[T_i] ≅ C_V for R = Γ(V, O_S). Each total-degree-n polynomial submodule is the R-span of coefficient extensions of integral degree-n polynomials: the monomial basis has monomials with coefficient 1, all of which lift. Transport this span equality through the polynomial isomorphism. Thus integralPolynomialMap preserves degrees, its images span each degree, and the positive-degree span implies the irrelevant-ideal condition. All algebraic span and substitution assertions are proved here from Mathlib polynomial and submodule lemmas.

proof.text: Construct β : R ⊗_Z Z[T_i] ≅ C_V by MvPolynomial.algebraTensorAlgEquiv followed by the preceding polynomial isomorphism. Its pure-tensor formula gives β(1 ⊗ a) = ψ_V(a). Apply [lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension] with the polynomial grading, the section grading as submodules, the coefficient-to-degree-zero maps, β, ψ_V, and the homogeneous span equality. Its uniqueness clause identifies its comparison with Proj.map ψ_V via Proj.map_preimage_basicOpen and Proj.awayι_comp_map. The canonical gradeIso in [def-nagata-relative-proj] changes back to the subgroup grading, and the affine-base and terminal-object isomorphisms give a cartesian square with projections integralMap and localBase. No flatness or nonzero-ring hypothesis is used.

proof.text: The standard free-basis inclusions and the symmetric-algebra inclusion in [def-nagata-relative-projective-space] are sheaf morphisms. Their naturality at 1 proves restriction of each coordinate. Naturality of the algebra unit proves restriction of coefficients. Polynomial ring-homomorphism extensionality therefore proves polynomial_restrict. Apply this calculation to integral coefficients and variables to get equality of the graded maps after restriction, and use Proj.map_comp to obtain integralMap_restrict. This is equality of the full scheme morphisms, hence also gives equality on their homogeneous-localization charts.

proof.text: For every affine V, pair its structural map to S with integralMap, after gradeIso, using [def-pc-fibre-product] to obtain comparisonChart into [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Pullback pasting with the cartesian square from step 2 proves that this chart is the inverse image of V. Both projections commute with further affine restriction by step 3 and the relative-Proj grading comparison. Apply relProjIsoOfIsPullback and relProjIsoOfIsPullback_hom_comp of [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists] to obtain θ and qθ = π. Its chart equation, together with restriction_ι of [def-nagata-relative-proj], shows affineToIntegral θ V = integralMap V. This proves the normalization and both restriction clauses. The cited universal property already performs the affine-refinement gluing and the inverse construction; no assumption on affine intersections or finiteness is added.

proof.text: For any other normalized θ′, the structural projections agree by their structure equations. The integral projections agree after every affine chart: the normalization fixes the underlying ring homomorphism to integralPolynomialMap, graded-ring-homomorphism extensionality fixes its graded map, and Proj.map_congr fixes its Proj morphism. Use the relative-Proj colimit characterization of [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists] to get equality of the global integral projections. Fibre-product hom_ext from [def-pc-fibre-product] gives equality of the hom maps and Iso.ext gives θ′ = θ.
